subject: ACME Health onboarding: candidate models, context needs & token-volume checkpoint
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME Health onboarding: candidate models, context needs & token-volume checkpoint

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our call I pulled together an initial model shortlist and very rough token-volume / context-length assumptions so we can align the implementation sprint and cost envelope before engineering kicks off. I don’t expect final answers yet — this is a checkpoint to make sure we’re solving for the right constraints.

Summary (short):
- Primary UX: clinical note summarization + structured extraction for claims intake. Typical input = user-submitted notes (free text), sometimes paste of multi-paragraph PDFs.
- Peak latency target: 400ms p50 for short summaries; 1.5s p95 acceptable for larger inputs.
- Privacy: must ingest PHI; customer will use Redwood Private (VPC) so data residency is US-only.

Initial model candidates we recommend testing: (purpose / tradeoffs)
1) Llama-2-13B-chat (8k) — good cost/quality balance for short-format summarization, fast on A100-style infra.
2) Falcon-40B-instruct (8k/16k) — stronger on instruction-following with structured output; higher cost but fewer hallucinations in our evals.
3) Mistral-Instruct-22B (8k) — good middle ground, strong on extraction tasks.
4) Long-context variant (Open model with 32k) — for edge workflows where PDFs are pasted; only use selectively with caching + chunking.

Token-volume assumptions (please confirm):
- Active users: 2,000 monthly active users (customer estimate)
- Avg daily requests (prod steady-state): 4,000 requests/day
- Request token profile: avg input 350 tokens, avg output 120 tokens => 470 tokens per request
- Estimated steady-state tokens/day = 4,000 * 470 = 1.88M tokens/day
- Peak day multiplier (marketing/seasonal): x3 => ~5.6M tokens/day

Ops notes / questions for you:
- Can you confirm the sample size: do you have 1–2 weeks of representative request logs we can use to validate token distribution? (Tom, Sarah — the CSV attached during the call looked high-level; sample convos would help.)
- Any hard latency SLAs for long-doc processing? If not, we’ll treat long-doc as async/queued.

Next steps I propose:
1) ACME to share 3–5 representative anonymized conversation samples and the Q1 usage CSV (attached if you already have it).
2) Redwood to run a quick spike (2 engineers, 3 days) comparing the 3 candidate models on your sample set and return: accuracy on extraction, avg latency, and cost-per-1M tokens for the config.
3) Agree on a canary rollout plan (1% traffic -> 10% -> 100%) plus fallback to a smaller model for peak events.

I’ve cc’d Monica and Grace for implementation and CS ops coordination. If this lineup looks reasonable we’ll schedule the spike for next week.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-usage-summary-q1.csv (summary), acme_sample_convos.json (sample convo stubs)
From: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Bennett <tbennett@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME Health onboarding: candidate models, context needs & token-volume checkpoint

Hi Irene —

Thanks — this is very helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications:
- The 2,000 MAU is a mid-year estimate; in Q3 we expect ramp to 5,000 MAU if the pilot converts. For spike planning, please assume a conservative peak of 10k MAU.
- We will absolutely provide 1 week of anonymized samples (I’ll scrub PHI and share). Expect the samples by end of day Wednesday.
- For long-docs: we currently have a small set of claims PDFs that are pasted by agents; those are not latency sensitive — async is fine.

I’m attaching the CSV export you mentioned and a short set of anonymized notes (acme_sample_convos.json). Let me know if you need additional metadata (user agent, upload size).

Best,
Sarah Lane
Head of Clinical Ops, ACME Health

Attachments: acme_sample_convos.json, acme-usage-summary-q1.csv
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@acmehealth.com>, Tom Bennett <tbennett@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Apr 2028 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME Health onboarding: candidate models, context needs & token-volume checkpoint

Grace / Monica —

Per Sarah’s note we’ll get sample convos tomorrow. I sketched a short evaluation plan below so CS / engineering can align on deliverables for the spike. Please comment inline if anything looks unrealistic.

Evaluation spike (goal: 3-day technical spike to pick a canary config):
Day 0 (prep): ingest samples into a test bucket, run a tokenization pass to profile token lengths and percentiles.
Day 1: run model inference across candidate models on the sample set (batch runs). Capture: exact-match fields for extraction, F1 for entities, avg latency (cold/hot), and cost per 1M tokens on our Dedicated infra.
Day 2: run stress test for synthetic peak (x3 and x10) with our batching profile; test fallback behavior where a smaller model is used after threshold.
Deliverable: short spreadsheet with results + recommended canary model and config (batch size, sequence length cap, quantization setting).

Operational constraints I want to call out:
- Because of PHI we’ll recommend Private deployment with KMS integration. That will change onboarding checklist (security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence).
- For long-doc flows we should design a chunking + KV-cache approach: chunk, generate metadata, then a final merging step for the summary. This avoids the need to run 32k context on every request.

Monica — can you confirm ETA for the spike engineers and whether we need a dedicated Dedicated pool for the benchmark runs? If so we should pull an initial capacity quote.

Thanks,
Irene
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Apr 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME Health onboarding: candidate models, context needs & token-volume checkpoint

Irene / Monica —

This plan looks good. A few operational clarifications from the implementation side:
- Engineers available for spike: Monday–Wednesday next week (Rohan and Priya from CS eng). I can carve 2 engineers for 3 days.
- Dedicated quote: to simulate production throughput for the stress runs, we’ll provision a small Dedicated pool (2x A100s) for 48 hours. I’ll ask Sales to issue a short-term quote — Monica, can you confirm pricing band for a 48h reserved pool?
- Telemetry: we’ll enable token-level tracing for the spike and add a trace-id to each request so we can map errors -> inputs. That will help with regression analysis.

Question for ACME: for the canary plan, do you want automated rollback after X% error increase, or manual rollback? We recommend automated rollback at 5% error delta vs baseline for the first canary.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lane <sarah.lane@acmehealth.com>, Tom Bennett <tbennett@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Apr 2028 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME Health onboarding: candidate models, context needs & token-volume checkpoint

All — quick sync and next steps from an implementation-schedule perspective:
- Received samples from Sarah on Wed; I reviewed tokenization pass — median input tokens = 320, 95th = 1,900 (these are usually long pasted notes). This confirms the hybrid approach (short model + async long-doc) is the right pattern.
- Spike start: Monday 2028-05-06 (Rohan & Priya). I booked the Dedicated 48h pool for the benchmark window (Sales issued short-term PO).
- Deliverables due EOD Wednesday (2028-05-08): benchmark spreadsheet, canary config, rollout plan, and cost projection for 1M / day and peak x3.
- Canary config recommendation (initial): Llama-2-13B-chat for 0–90% requests, Falcon-40B-instruct reserved for extraction-heavy flows where higher accuracy is required (selective routing). Use quantized 4-bit for Llama to reduce cost.

Action items:
1) Sarah / Tom: confirm sample anonymization is complete and that you’re ok with Redwood running these tests in the Private environment (KMS will be used).
2) Monica: confirm engineer allocation and attach the pricing note for the 48h Dedicated pool to HUBSPOT-ACME-2387.
3) Grace: please capture the automated rollback threshold in the rollout doc (suggest 5% error delta).

I’ll follow up with a short kickoff calendar invite for Monday.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Implementation, Redwood Inference
